## 🎯 Main Idea
- End-to-end walkthrough of a full enterprise penetration test against INLANEFREIGHT, from external recon to full Active Directory domain compromise.
- Ties together the whole Penetration Tester path: external gathering, service/web exploitation, initial access, pivoting, lateral movement, AD attacks, post-exploitation, and closeout.
- Emphasizes methodology and workflow (a repeatable kill-chain) rather than any single technique.

## 💥 Attack / Exploit Vectors (Engagement Phases)

### Scenario & Kickoff
- Project kickoff: confirm scope, rules of engagement, and start of testing.

### External Information Gathering
- Passive/active recon of public-facing assets, DNS, and subdomains.
- **Commands**
  - `sudo nmap --open ...` — scan external hosts for live services
  - `dig axfr @<ns> inlanefreight.local` — attempt DNS zone transfer
  - `fierce` / `dnsenum` — DNS and subdomain enumeration
  - `curl -s -I http://10.129.203.101 -H "HOST: dev.inlanefreight.local"` — virtual host probing

### Service Enumeration & Exploitation
- Enumerate listening services (FTP, SSH, email/SMTP) and exploit misconfigurations.
- **Commands**
  - `sudo nmap -sV -sC -p25 10.129.203.101` — enumerate SMTP/mail service
  - FTP anonymous access and SSH checks on identified hosts

### Web Enumeration & Exploitation
- Enumerate many virtual hosts (blog, careers, dev, gitlab, vpn, shopdev2, monitoring) and exploit the weakest.
- **Commands**
  - `eyewitness -f ilfreight_subdomains ...` — screenshot web apps
  - `gobuster dir -u http://dev.inlanefreight.local -w <wordlist>` — directory brute force
  - `ffuf -w <wordlist> ...` — fuzz paths/parameters/vhosts
  - `curl http://ir.inlanefreight.local` — manual inspection
  - `hydra -l admin ...` — brute-force a web login
  - command injection / RCE on a vulnerable monitoring app to get code execution

### Initial Access
- Convert a web/service exploit into an interactive reverse shell on a DMZ host.
- **Commands**
  - Craft a reverse shell payload and catch with a listener (nc/msf)

### Post-Exploitation Persistence & Local Priv Esc (DMZ)
- Stabilize access, escalate locally to root, and establish persistence on the foothold.
- **Commands**
  - Local privesc enumeration (sudo rights, SUID, cron) to get root
  - Add SSH keys / accounts for persistence

### Internal Information Gathering & Pivoting
- Pivot from the DMZ into the internal 172.16.8.0/23 network; enumerate hosts and AD.
- **Commands**
  - `ssh -D 8081 -i dmz01_key root@10.129.203.111` — SOCKS dynamic port forward (proxychains)
  - `proxychains nmap -sT -p 21,22,80,8080 172.16.8.120` — scan internal hosts through proxy
  - Metasploit `autoroute` / `socks_proxy` — alternate pivot setup
  - `proxychains enum4linux 172.16.8.x` / `rpcclient` — SMB/AD enumeration
  - SMB NULL session — anonymous AD enumeration
  - Enumerate Tomcat (172.16.8.50) and DotNetNuke/DNN (172.16.8.20)

### Internal Exploitation & Privilege Escalation
- Exploit DotNetNuke (DNN) for code execution, then escalate on the Windows host.
- **Commands**
  - `ssh -i dmz01_key -R 172.16.8.120:443:0.0.0.0:7000 root@10.129.203.111 -vN` — reverse port forward for callback
  - `secretsdump.py LOCAL -system SYSTEM.SAVE -sam SAM.SAVE -security SECURITY.SAVE` — dump local hashes
  - `proxychains crackmapexec smb 172.16.8.20 --local-auth -u admin -H <hash>` — pass-the-hash check

### Lateral Movement
- Move across the domain via share hunting, Kerberoasting, and password spraying.
- **Commands**
  - `GetUserSPNs.py` — request service tickets (Kerberoasting)
  - `hashcat -m 13100 ilfreight_spns <wordlist>` — crack TGS hashes
  - `proxychains crackmapexec smb 172.16.8.3 -u ssmalls -p 'Str0...'` — password spray / validate creds
  - `proxychains smbclient` — share hunting for sensitive files
  - `nmap -sT -p 5985 172.16.8.50` + `proxychains evil-winrm ...` — WinRM access
  - `ssh -i dmz01_key -L 13389:172.16.8.20:3389 root@10.129.203.111` — local forward for RDP

### Active Directory Compromise
- Escalate from domain foothold to Domain Admin / Domain Controller.
- **Commands**
  - `mimikatz.exe` — dump credentials / tickets from memory
  - DCSync / NTDS extraction to obtain all domain hashes

### Post-Exploitation
- Full domain takeover actions: NTDS cracking, security audit, double pivot, exfil, trust attacks.
- **Commands**
  - `secretsdump.py` / crack NTDS with hashcat — domain password analysis
  - Double pivot to MGMT01 (deeper segmented network)
  - BloodHound — Active Directory security audit / attack-path mapping
  - Data exfiltration simulation and attacking domain trusts

### Engagement Closeout
- Wrap-up and professional delivery.
- **Key points**
  - Attack-path recap and structuring findings
  - Post-engagement cleanup (remove tools, accounts, artifacts)
  - Client communication and internal project closeout

## 🛠️ Key Tools & Concepts
- `nmap`, `gobuster`, `ffuf`, `eyewitness`, `hydra` — recon & web enumeration
- `proxychains` + SSH tunneling (`-D`, `-L`, `-R`) / Metasploit autoroute — pivoting
- `enum4linux`, `rpcclient`, `crackmapexec`, `smbclient` — SMB/AD enumeration
- `GetUserSPNs.py`, `secretsdump.py`, `evil-winrm`, `mimikatz` — AD attacks & cred dumping
- `hashcat` / `john` — offline password cracking
- `BloodHound` — AD attack-path analysis
- Kill chain: recon → exploit → foothold → pivot → lateral movement → DA → post-exploit → report

## 🛡️ Mitigations
- Reduce external attack surface; patch and harden public-facing web/service apps.
- Network segmentation to limit DMZ-to-internal pivoting.
- Strong Kerberos service-account passwords (defeat Kerberoasting); enforce password policy to stop spraying.
- Least privilege, disable SMB NULL sessions, protect LSASS/NTDS, and monitor for lateral movement.
